reasons.reader_question: The ending asks a clear question. Devan has cleared the only eye on the ledge, so has he made himself her prey? It sharpens the beat's 'protect her or trap her' question, but the last image is a routine exit, so the question has less pull than it could.
reasons.change: His knowledge changes: her cover deflects every personal question, the scars mean a childhood in the guild, and she has a will of her own. Power changes too: he gives up the wall above his window and his own safety.
reasons.romance_movement: The value shift lands for a new, specific reason. She tears trousseau cloth for a goat-boy and knows his mother's name, which echoes Asha's slate. He goes from 'the thing that had been sent' to 'a person'.
reasons.shown_chemistry: The terrace exchange of questions for questions is good sparring, and 'the first time all morning she had sounded like herself' is a sharp responsive observation. But the page shows no bodily or personal desire. It shows suspicion and dawning respect only.
reasons.character_logic: Devan's choice not to stop Janu's story, and his witness-rule reason for pulling the sentry, are smart and in character. The weak spot is Neela: a guild-trained liar volunteers 'a childhood burn' here, and the record has her telling the same man 'a fall from a cart' a week later.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Pulling the sentry costs a guard on the wall nearest the ford raids. It plants a question in Muthu, the queen's informant. It also leaves Devan alone with an assassin and no witness. The cold thought at the end names that cost.
reasons.prose: The prose is clean of banned phrases and AI tells, uses few em dashes, and has strong concrete detail (berry sinkers, wet sacks and cloves). There are clunks: the inverted 'Her breaths he counted until she slept', the echo of 'come back shaking' and 'come to the bed shaking' in the first lines, and a tangled paragraph about what Muthu knows.
reasons.continuity: The chapter is consistent with ch4's dawn (F308, F309), the sentry placed above the window (F052, F065, F314), the bar left for her to lift, the classroom resin at twenty (F041), Asha's slate (F063), Janu finding the body (F066), the hilt toward her (F038) and Kannan's age. Janu's stories are held for ch9, which follows the secret map.

fixes: At '"A childhood burn," she said, lightly. "I was clumsy."' (Irrational behaviour, continuity risk): a trained liar does not use two different stories for the same scars with the same man. F200 has her say 'a fall from a cart' in the second week. Change the line to '"A fall from a cart," she said, lightly. "I was small, and clumsy."' Keep Devan's 'It was no child's fall'. Update F311 so the ch22 back-reference reads as her repeating this lie when he asks.

At 'Then one day there had been a captain on his knees with his hands open' (Contrived delays in reverse, an early spend of a planted secret): this gives away the core image of the ch21 disclosure ladder, the kneeling, surrendering captain. The next paragraph ('Muthu had been there. He knew what had happened. He had never been told...') is tangled. Cut it to 'Then there had been the ford, and one strike, and a silence.' Rewrite the next paragraph as: 'Muthu had been at the ford. He had seen what Devan's hand did. He had never seen what it did to Devan, and Devan meant to keep it that way.'

At 'Soft as a dropped cloth, her weight landed on the ledge.' (weak chapter-ending hook): she does this every night, so the last image repeats action instead of interrupting it. Keep the cold thought. Then add one story-caused beat specific to tonight: her weight comes onto the ledge and stops. No resin scent yet, no claws on stone. She stays crouched in the open window and listens to the bare rampart above her, and he understands she has noticed that the sentry is gone. End on her stillness, which leaves 'what will she do with the gap he made?' open. This fits F079, where she later 'no longer calls it luck'.
reader_question: By pulling the one sentry who could see the ledge, has Devan just cleared the way for the woman he's protecting to kill him?
new_facts_assessment: F350 (she turns back in the yard and comes up the stair door wrapped in a stable saddle-blanket) is necessary. It follows from ch4's ending and F309, and with the hounds kennelled it is plausible. F351 is also necessary and consistent. Tracking her by paw-marks gives his stated motive ('watch who she reports to') a practical method, and the 'truer reason' applies Rule 2 correctly, setting up F278 and F344. Retiring F064 is correct, because it has him leave the bar against the wall, which contradicts F065, F314 and this chapter. Trimming F310's 'inner wrist only' is correct, because F014 puts scars at the throat as well. One flag: F311 ('a childhood burn' as her first lie) gives Neela two different cover stories for the same scars to the same man within a week (see F200). Either align the lie or note in F200 that he catches the discrepancy.
